elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 permits Ono, the Customer, to terminate “for any reason,” which creates a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right at any time during the committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly permits Ono to terminate “at any time” and removes the delayed First Commercial Sale triggers.

elements.element: Customer must give 30 days' advance written notice of termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause requires ninety (90), rather than 30, days' advance written notice.

elements.element: Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires any refund of prepaid fees following Ono's convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The rendered language grants the convenience right only to Ono. Array's stated termination rights are tied to Ono's breach or commercialization of a Competing Product, not convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience at any time during the committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 permits Ono to terminate “at any time” and “for any reason,” without the prior delayed eligibility trigger.

elements.element: Customer must give between 60 and 90 days' advance notice of termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 requires ninety (90) days' advance written notice, which is within the permitted 60–90 day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee charged to Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The supplied operative language imposes no early-termination fee, so the condition for applying the fee cap is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, it may take effect only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not grant Array any termination-for-convenience right; Array's identified termination rights are cause-based. The conditional restriction is therefore satisfied by the absence of such a right.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, Vendor must give 90 days' advance notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not grant Array a termination-for-convenience right, so the notice condition for such a right is not triggered.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback by granting Ono an at-any-time convenience right on 90 days' written notice, with no early-termination fee or Array convenience right. It misses the preferred 30-day period and pro-rata refund. It is not minimal and does not fully preserve the original commercial scope because it additionally creates a Product-by-Product termination right, whereas the original clause contemplated termination of the Agreement without that partial-termination option. The drafting is otherwise understandable, but the new partial-termination mechanism is not accompanied by provisions addressing allocation of rights, obligations, payments, or termination effects for retained versus terminated Products.
